packet.headline_seed: UN pauses Strait of Hormuz evacuation plan after cargo ship attacked
packet.description_seed: The ship was reportedly struck by an "unknown projectile" near Oman but no casualties were reported.

what: UN pauses Strait of Hormuz evacuation plan after cargo ship attacked

clean_source_blocks.text: The UN's International Maritime Organization (IMO) has paused the planned evacuation of more than 11,000 sailors stranded in the Strait of Hormuz after a cargo ship passing through the waterway was attacked. IMO chief Arsenio Dominguez said several boats had already been evacuated, but the agency wanted to ensure that "necessary safety guarantees" would continue to be in place. The British maritime security agency UKMTO reported on Thursday that a ship had been struck 7.5 nautical miles southeast of Oman's port of Dahit by "an unknown projectile". No casualties were reported. Maritime risk management firm Vanguard said the ship, Singapore-flagged Ever Lovely, continued through strait despite the attack. Hundreds of ships and thousands of sailors have been stranded in the Gulf since February because of the US-Israel war against Iran.
The ship was reportedly struck by an "unknown projectile" near Oman but no casualties were reported.

DUBAI, United Arab Emirates (AP) — A United Nations agency paused the evacuation of ships through the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday after the British military said a vessel was hit by a projectile off the coast of Oman following the passage of several tankers that used a route backed by the U.N. The head of the International Maritime Organization said the plan to move stranded ships out of the Persian Gulf through the strait will be on hold until the agency can confirm safety guarantees for the ships on the evacuation list and in the region. It was unclear who launched the projectile or the type of vessel that was targeted. The report of a strike came hours after Iran threatened vessels to stop using the route through the strait without Tehran’s permission.

The UN evacuation effort was only announced on Tuesday following the reopening of the strait, with Dominguez saying the "large-scale operation" had the cooperation of Iran, Oman, the US, other coastal states in the region and the maritime industry. Dominguez said in a statement on Thursday that the vessel that was attacked "did not transit under IMO's evacuation framework". "I have always reiterated that the safety of the seafarers remains paramount. Therefore, to ensure a coordinated approach and navigational safety, the evacuation plan will be paused until further clarity is obtained," he added. Ship-tracking website MarineTraffic, said the Ever Lovely entered the Strait using the southern route on Thursday morning and exited on the east side at around 15:30 local time (16:30 BST). Vanguard also reported no assistance was required.

payload.title: YK keskeytti Hormuzinsalmen evakuointisuunnitelman rahtialukseen osuneen iskun jälkeen
payload.summary: YK:n merenkulkujärjestö IMO on pysäyttänyt suunnitelman yli 11 000 merimiehen evakuoimiseksi Hormuzinsalmen kautta, kun Omanin rannikon lähellä kulkenut rahtialus osui tuntemattomaan ammukseen. Henkilövahingoista ei ole ilmoitettu.
payload.content:
YK:n alainen Kansainvälinen merenkulkujärjestö IMO on keskeyttänyt suunnitellun evakuointioperaation Hormuzinsalmessa sen jälkeen, kun alueella kulkenut rahtialus joutui iskun kohteeksi Omanin rannikon edustalla. Operaation oli tarkoitus auttaa yli 11 000:ta merimiestä, jotka ovat jääneet odottamaan pääsyä Persianlahdelta salmen kautta ulos. Iskussa ei ilmoitettu henkilövahingoista.

## Turvatakuut tarkistetaan uudelleen

IMO:n pääsihteeri Arsenio Dominguez sanoi, että useita aluksia oli jo evakuoitu, mutta järjestön on varmistettava, että tarvittavat turvatakuut ovat edelleen voimassa. Hänen mukaansa merenkulkijoiden turvallisuus on ensisijainen asia, ja evakuointisuunnitelma pidetään tauolla, kunnes tilanteesta saadaan lisää selvyyttä ja navigointiturvallisuus voidaan varmistaa koordinoidusti.

Britannian meriturvallisuusviranomainen UKMTO ilmoitti torstaina, että alus oli saanut osuman noin 7,5 meripeninkulmaa Omanin Dahitin satamasta kaakkoon. Osuman aiheuttajaksi kuvattiin tuntematon ammus. Vielä ei ole selvää, kuka ammuksen laukaisi tai minkä tyyppiseen alukseen isku tarkalleen kohdistui.

## Ever Lovely jatkoi matkaansa

Merenkulun riskienhallintayhtiö Vanguardin mukaan kyseessä oli Singaporen lipun alla kulkeva Ever Lovely. Yhtiön mukaan alus jatkoi matkaansa Hormuzinsalmen läpi iskusta huolimatta, eikä se tarvinnut apua. Alusseurantasivusto MarineTrafficin mukaan Ever Lovely saapui salmeen eteläistä reittiä torstaiaamuna ja poistui sen itäpuolelle noin kello 15.30 paikallista aikaa.

Dominguez korosti, että iskun kohteeksi joutunut alus ei kulkenut IMO:n evakuointijärjestelyn puitteissa. Evakuointihanke oli julkistettu vasta tiistaina salmen uudelleenavaamisen jälkeen. Sen kerrottiin perustuvan yhteistyöhön Iranin, Omanin, Yhdysvaltojen, alueen muiden rannikkovaltioiden ja merenkulkualan kanssa.

## Taustalla laajempi seisokki

Persianlahdelle on jäänyt helmikuusta lähtien satoja aluksia ja tuhansia merimiehiä Yhdysvaltojen ja Israelin Irania vastaan käymän sodan vuoksi. Torstain iskusta kerrottiin vain tunteja sen jälkeen, kun Iran oli uhannut aluksia, jotka käyttäisivät salmen kautta kulkevaa reittiä ilman Teheranin lupaa.

The UN's International Maritime Organization (IMO) has paused the planned evacuation of more than 11,000 sailors stranded in the Strait of Hormuz after a cargo ship passing through the waterway was attacked. IMO chief Arsenio Dominguez said several boats had already been evacuated, but the agency wanted to ensure that "necessary safety guarantees" would continue to be in place. The British maritime security agency UKMTO reported on Thursday that a ship had been struck 7.5 nautical miles southeast of Oman's port of Dahit by "an unknown projectile". No casualties were reported. Maritime risk management firm Vanguard said the ship, Singapore-flagged Ever Lovely, continued through strait despite the attack. Hundreds of ships and thousands of sailors have been stranded in the Gulf since February because of the US-Israel war against Iran.

The ship was reportedly struck by an "unknown projectile" near Oman but no casualties were reported.

DUBAI, United Arab Emirates (AP) — A United Nations agency paused the evacuation of ships through the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday after the British military said a vessel was hit by a projectile off the coast of Oman following the passage of several tankers that used a route backed by the U.N. The head of the International Maritime Organization said the plan to move stranded ships out of the Persian Gulf through the strait will be on hold until the agency can confirm safety guarantees for the ships on the evacuation list and in the region. It was unclear who launched the projectile or the type of vessel that was targeted. The report of a strike came hours after Iran threatened vessels to stop using the route through the strait without Tehran’s permission.

The UN evacuation effort was only announced on Tuesday following the reopening of the strait, with Dominguez saying the "large-scale operation" had the cooperation of Iran, Oman, the US, other coastal states in the region and the maritime industry. Dominguez said in a statement on Thursday that the vessel that was attacked "did not transit under IMO's evacuation framework". "I have always reiterated that the safety of the seafarers remains paramount. Therefore, to ensure a coordinated approach and navigational safety, the evacuation plan will be paused until further clarity is obtained," he added. Ship-tracking website MarineTraffic, said the Ever Lovely entered the Strait using the southern route on Thursday morning and exited on the east side at around 15:30 local time (16:30 BST). Vanguard also reported no assistance was required.
